title: Quasi-coherent etale cohomology comparison natural in scheme pullback
statement:
Let $X,Y$ be quasi-compact separated schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $g:Y\to X$ a scheme morphism, and $F$ and $G$ quasi-coherent modules on $X$ and $Y$ respectively [pqf-def-coherent, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $F_{\mathrm{et}},G_{\mathrm{et}}$ be their associated additive etale sheaves [def-sc-etale-qcoherent-module]. Fix the size convention [def-weil-size-convention]: for schemes in universe $u$, use the common coefficient category $\mathrm{AddCommGrp}_{u+1}$ of the recorded inverse-image and cohomology-pullback functors. Set $L$ to sectionwise $\operatorname{ULift}^{u+1}$, transporting addition and every restriction map. This is the common-lift formulation of the source comparison, rather than quantification over the identity and arbitrary further coefficient-universe lifts. For every $q\ge0$ there are canonical additive isomorphisms
$$c^q_{X,F}:H^q(X_{\mathrm{et}},L(F_{\mathrm{et}}))\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(X,F),$$
where the right side is Zariski module cohomology [pqf-def-cohomology] and the left side is abelian etale cohomology [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. In degree zero $c^0$ is $\operatorname{ULift.down}$ on sections, using the canonical tensor-pullback unit to identify sections on the terminal etale object and the degree-zero right-derived global-sections comparison. These isomorphisms are simultaneous for all such schemes and modules and natural as follows. For every module morphism $\psi:g^*F\to G$ [def-pc-module-pullback], let $\psi_{\mathrm{et}}:g^{-1}L(F_{\mathrm{et}})\to L(G_{\mathrm{et}})$ be adjoint to the sectionwise map sending a section on an etale $U\to X$ to its structural pullback on $U\times_XY$, followed by the pullback of $\psi$. Then
$$c^q_{Y,G}\circ H^q(\psi_{\mathrm{et}})\circ g_{\mathrm{et}}^*=\psi_{\mathrm{Zar}}^*\circ c^q_{X,F},$$
where $g_{\mathrm{et}}^*$ is [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback] and $\psi_{\mathrm{Zar}}^*$ is the module cohomology map of the adjoint $F\to g_*G$ [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap]. In particular, for $g=\mathrm{id}$ and multiplication by $a\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$ these comparisons intertwine multiplication by $a$ on both cohomology groups (or by its lift on the left). The lifted associated sheaf and module-morphism action are the constructions recorded in [def-pbc-canonical-coherent-etale-comparison]; only those constructions are used here, with no properness or base-field restriction.

source.place: Tag 03P2, label theorem-zariski-fpqc-quasi-coherent, separated-case affine-cover proof; canonical comparison naturality and its sectionwise coefficient-universe lift

proof.text: Choose a finite affine open cover $\mathcal U=(U_i)$ of $X$. More generally any finite open covering admits a finite affine refinement by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-scheme-cofinal-finite-coverings]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-separated-affine-open-intersection] with $A=\mathbf Z$ to the separated structural map to $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, and iterate: every nonempty tuple intersection $U_{i_0\ldots i_p}$ is affine. This uses separatedness, not merely quasi-separatedness. The same conclusions hold for $Y$. Open intersections are the tuple fibre products in the etale site by [lem-weil-pbc-zariski-etale-inclusion-morphism-of-sites].

Put $E=L(F_{\mathrm{et}})$. For $L=\mathrm{id}$ and an affine tuple intersection $j:W\hookrightarrow X$, [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits], clause (2), says that $F|_W$ is quasi-coherent. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology-over-open], $H^r(W,F_{\mathrm{et}})$ computed over the object $W$ of $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ is canonically $H^r(W_{\mathrm{et}},(F|_W)_{\mathrm{et}})$. Apply [lem-sc-etale-affine-qcoherent] to $W$ and $F|_W$ to make this zero for $r>0$. For a coefficient lift use [new-etale-finite-affine-cech-basis] with the affine objects of $X_{\mathrm{et}}$: its finite affine families are cofinal and closed under tuple fibre products. On each such family [new-etale-affine-tensor-cech-vanishing] gives positive Cech vanishing for the lifted tensor-section sheaf, which is precisely $E$ by [def-sc-etale-qcoherent-module]. The explicit/categorical Cech identification is [lem-weil-pbc-site-cech-mathlib-comparison]. Thus all three hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-cech-vanishing-criterion] hold and $H^r(W,E)=0$ for every affine etale object $W$ and $r>0$. The basis and criterion are used in the common larger universe, where the site skeleton, finite indices and lifted groups are small. No preservation of injectives by coefficient lift is asserted. Repeat for $G$ on $Y$.

source.place: Tag 03P2, affine acyclicity; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 03F9, lemma-cech-vanish-collection

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-acyclic-cech-edge-compatibility] and step 2, the normalized etale edge $e_{\mathcal U,E}:\check H^q(\mathcal U,E)\to H^q(X_{\mathrm{et}},E)$ is an isomorphism. For module cohomology use the canonical comparison [def-sc-module-cech-comparison]: its restriction augmentation $\alpha$ induces an isomorphism, and [lem-sc-module-cech-beta-affine-quasi-iso] makes its coefficient augmentation $\beta$ a quasi-isomorphism on this affine-intersection family. Hence its module edge $m_{\mathcal U,F}$ is an isomorphism. On every tuple, the associated etale sheaf evaluates to $\Gamma(U_{\mathbf i},F)$, or its lift. Define the cochain isomorphism $d_{\mathcal U,F}:\check C(\mathcal U,E)\to\check C(\mathcal U,F)$ coordinatewise by identity or $\operatorname{ULift.down}$. It commutes with the differential: each signed face restriction commutes with down by the definition of $L$, and down preserves addition. It is invertible coordinatewise by identity or up. Set $c^q_{X,F}=m_{\mathcal U,F}\,H^q(d_{\mathcal U,F})\,e_{\mathcal U,E}^{-1}$. In degree zero both edges identify a glued section with that section, so $c^0$ has the stated normalization. The two total-complex index conventions give the same normalized edge: with Cech degree $t$ and resolution degree $r$, multiplication by $(-1)^{tr}$ identifies the differential $d_C+(-1)^t d_I$ with $d_I+(-1)^r d_C$ [def-sp-double-complex-total]. It is the identity on both augmentation axes, so it changes neither $H(\alpha)^{-1}H(\beta)$ nor its degree-zero normalization.

source.place: Tag 03P2, separated-case equal Cech complexes; cohomology.tex Tag 01EQ, lemma-cech-cohomology

proof.text: The definition in step 3 is independent of the affine covering. Given two finite affine covers, take a finite affine refinement of their intersection covering by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-scheme-cofinal-finite-coverings]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-cech-refinement-square] with the identity site morphism and coefficient identity, first for etale abelian sheaves and then for Zariski modules. Both normalized edges commute with the refinement cochain maps. Coordinatewise down commutes with these maps because they only restrict sections and reindex tuples. For an affine refinement all four edges are invertible by step 3; therefore the two composites defining $c$ agree after cancellation. This constructs the simultaneous canonical family without a choice depending on a morphism or a scalar.

source.place: Tag 01FD, lemma-functoriality-cech, identity-morphism refinement case; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 03AX

proof.text: For $g:Y\to X$, choose a finite affine refinement $\mathcal V=(V_j)$ of the open cover $(g^{-1}U_i)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-scheme-cofinal-finite-coverings], with index map $r$ and $V_j\subseteq g^{-1}U_{r(j)}$. These inverse images need not be affine; only $\mathcal V$ and $\mathcal U$ are used as acyclic covers. The etale base-change functor defines a morphism of sites by [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-exact]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-cech-refinement-square] to its adjoint coefficient map $E\to g_*L(G_{\mathrm{et}})$: the resulting cohomology map is exactly $H^q(\psi_{\mathrm{et}})g_{\mathrm{et}}^*$, with the resolution/unit normalization of [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback]. Apply the same lemma to the ringed Zariski sites and the module map $F\to g_*G$ adjoint to $\psi$; its resolution construction is the map $\psi_{\mathrm{Zar}}^*$ of [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap]. The two refinement cochain maps have the same coordinates: for a tuple $\mathbf j$, structurally pull back $s_{r(\mathbf j)}$, apply $\psi$, and restrict to $V_{\mathbf j}$. Coordinatewise down commutes with this formula since the lifted map is $\operatorname{ULift.map}$ of that additive map. Thus $d_{\mathcal V,G}\gamma_{\mathrm{et}}=\gamma_{\mathrm{Zar}}d_{\mathcal U,F}$. Insert the two edge squares into the formula of step 3 and cancel the invertible etale edges to obtain $c^q_{Y,G}H^q(\psi_{\mathrm{et}})g_{\mathrm{et}}^*=\psi_{\mathrm{Zar}}^*c^q_{X,F}$.

source.place: Tag 01FD, tuple formula and augmented comparison diagram; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 03AX

proof.text: Take $g=\mathrm{id}_X$, $G=F$, and $\psi$ multiplication by $a$. The section formula of [def-sc-etale-qcoherent-module] sends a tuple section to its product with $a|_{U_{\mathbf i}}$, or to its lifted product. The identity pullback is identity on cohomology by [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial], clause 4. Step 5 now reads $c^q_{X,F}H^q(\mu_a)=H^q(a\cdot-)c^q_{X,F}$, which is the final clause.
